title: Bench Verification Checklist - Predictive Thermal Guard
purpose: Track real hardware verification so NOTES.md can be filled with actual measurements instead of placeholders.
rules: Only record measurements you actually took.
If a step fails, record what failed and what you tried, not just the eventual fix.
Do not ask ChatGPT to invent NOTES.md values.
Update status fields as you go: 'not_started', 'in_progress', 'done', 'blocked'.
equipment_needed: Reference thermometer (phone IR thermometer or lab thermometer)
Low-voltage safe heat source (NOT mains equipment)

sessions.name: Host bus and mux
sessions.goal: Confirm ESP32 can see the TCA9548A on I2C before any sensors are attached.
steps: Wire ESP32 to TCA9548A per hardware/WIRING.md (host side only)
Tie A0/A1/A2 to GND so mux address is 0x70
Power ESP32 over USB
Multimeter: measure 3V3 to GND, expect ~3.3V
Multimeter: measure SDA and SCL to GND with bus idle, expect ~3.3V (pulled high)
Flash a basic Arduino I2C scanner sketch
Confirm scanner reports a device at 0x70
troubleshooting_if_not_found: confirm 3.3V vs 5V logic level matches ESP32 board

sessions.name: First MLX90614
sessions.goal: Confirm one real sensor gives sane, cross-checkable readings through the mux.
steps: Wire one MLX90614 to mux channel 0 per hardware/WIRING.md
Flash firmware/src/main.cpp, open serial monitor
Confirm boot log reports 'MLX90614 ready on mux channel 0'
Point sensor at a known surface and simultaneously check with reference thermometer
Run for 10 minutes, count any 'read failed' lines
sessions.notes: MLX90614 accuracy is ~+/-0.5C in ideal conditions but depends heavily on emissivity and distance. A few degrees off vs. reference is normal - record it honestly.

sessions.name: Multiple sensors and MQTT
sessions.goal: Confirm mux correctly switches between sensors and MQTT delivery is reliable.
steps: Add 2nd (and 3rd/4th if available) MLX90614 on remaining mux channels
Start Mosquitto broker locally
In separate terminal: mosquitto_sub -v -t 'thermal-fault-guard/+/temperature'
Flash and run firmware, confirm all connected channels report 'ready' at boot
Watch serial monitor and mosquitto_sub output for at least 5 minutes
Test Wi-Fi reconnect: power-cycle router or move ESP32 out of range briefly
Test MQTT reconnect: stop and restart Mosquitto broker while ESP32 runs

sessions.name: End-to-end fault detection
sessions.goal: Confirm the rolling-average detector in backend/monitor.py flags a real temperature change.
sessions.safety_note: Use a low-voltage, controlled heat source only. Never point sensors at mains-powered equipment or exposed wiring.
steps: Start monitor: thermal-monitor --broker localhost --csv temperature_log.csv
Let one channel sit at stable baseline for at least 2 minutes (needs 8+ samples)
Introduce heat source near that sensor
Watch for [FAULT] line in monitor output
Open dashboard (thermal-dashboard --csv temperature_log.csv) and confirm row turns red with a marked point on the plot

after_all_sessions: Update README 'Current status' section to reflect what's actually verified
Add real photo: hardware/photos/breadboard-overview.jpg, replace placeholder note
Fix hardware/WIRING.md or KiCad drawing if reality differed from the draft
Commit separately with an honest message, e.g. 'bench: sessions 1-3 + fault trial completed, see NOTES.md'
If any step failed and stayed unresolved, leave it documented as an open problem in NOTES.md rather than omitting it
